sourcedFrom: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed (2003 (archive capture date; the document is undated on its face))
cleanIntro: Charter's own procedure for the Undercover. It is a five-shot .38 Special double-action revolver with a transfer-bar safety, and the routine job needs no disassembly at all — Charter says so. ⛔ Two things on this gun are Charter's own and not generic revolver advice: the cleaning interval is every session OR 50 ROUNDS, whichever comes first, with a screw-tightness check in the same breath; and ⛔ .38 SPECIAL +P AMMUNITION IS NOT RECOMMENDED IN THIS REVOLVER by the maker's own footnote.

steps.title: Swing the cylinder out and look — every time
steps.action: Press forward on the cylinder latch on the left side of the frame, swing the cylinder out, and confirm every chamber is empty before anything else happens.
steps.prose: Charter's point is that a swing-out revolver is a safer design than most pistols precisely BECAUSE you can see the chambers — and that the advantage is worth nothing unless you actually look, every time you pick the gun up.
steps.quote: The double action, swing out cylinder revolver is a safer design than most pistols. But it is still necessary to swing out the cylinder and check to see if the gun is loaded anytime the gun is handled.
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, printed p.2

steps.title: Hammer down, trigger free to return forward
steps.action: Leave the hammer uncocked and resting against the frame, and make sure the trigger is free to return fully forward.
steps.prose: That is the state the transfer-bar safety is designed around. A trigger held part-way back by grit or a holster is a trigger that is not at rest, and Charter calls it out as its own condition.
steps.quote: Always carry the revolver with the hammer uncocked and resting against the frame. Always insure that the trigger is free to return to its forward, at rest position.
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, printed p.2

steps.title: ⛔ Uncocking a cocked hammer — thumb first, trigger second
steps.action: If the hammer is cocked and you decide not to fire: hold the frame in your left hand ahead of the trigger guard; hold the hammer securely with your right thumb so it cannot move; squeeze the trigger with your right index finger and let the hammer move forward SLIGHTLY under thumb control; release the trigger; then ease the hammer down.
steps.prose: ⛔ The order matters and the thumb never leaves the hammer. Release the trigger BEFORE lowering the hammer the rest of the way — that is what puts the mechanism back in its safe state rather than riding the hammer down on a live trigger.
steps.quote: Release the trigger, then ease the hammer
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — UNCOCKING THE HAMMER, printed p.4
steps.warn: The above sequence must be done carefully. If your thumb slips while the trigger is pulled to the rear, the hammer will fly forward and the gun will fire.

steps.title: Bore and chambers clear, and dry of excess oil
steps.action: With the cylinder out and the gun empty, check that the bore and every chamber are unobstructed and free of grease or excess oil.
steps.prose: ⛔ Charter puts rust and corrosion in the same sentence as an obstruction, and means it literally: enough of either generates extreme overpressure on firing. This is why the cleaning below ends dry-then-lightly-oiled and not simply oiled.
steps.quote: Rust and corrosion can cause a sufficient obstruction to generate extreme overpressure upon firing, which may result in possible structural failure and serious injury to the shooter or bystanders.
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, printed p.2

steps.title: Solvent through the bore and every chamber
steps.action: Wipe the revolver down with a nitro/powder solvent and a soft cloth, then run the solvent through the barrel bore and the cylinder chambers on a flannel patch and cleaning rod. A correctly sized bristle brush if the patches will not do it.
steps.prose: Every chamber, not just the bore — a revolver's chambers are six short barrels and they foul at the mouth where the case ends.
steps.quote: After unloading the gun, the barrel bore and cylinder chambers should be cleaned with this solvent on a flannel patch and cleaning rod.
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — CLEANING, printed p.4

steps.title: ⛔ Every session or 50 rounds — and check the screws
steps.action: Clean after every shooting session or every 50 rounds, whichever comes first, and check all pins and screws for tightness while you are there.
steps.prose: ⛔ Fifty rounds is a short interval by modern standards and it is Charter's own. The screw check is in the same sentence for a reason: a revolver shoots its own sideplate and grip screws loose, and a wandering crane screw is how a cylinder starts binding.
steps.quote: This cleaning should be performed after every shooting session, or 50 rounds, whichever comes first; also check all Pins and Screws for tightness.
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — CLEANING, printed p.4

steps.title: Wipe the solvent off, then a light film of oil
steps.action: Wipe the whole gun free of solvent and give it a light film of rust-preventing oil. Wipe the grips DRY. The critical moving parts can be lightly oiled without taking anything apart.
steps.prose: Grips dry, metal lightly oiled — oiled grips are a gun that turns in the hand, and on wood they lift the finish.
steps.aside: All critical moving parts of your revolver can be lightly oiled without disassembling the gun.
steps.quote: After cleaning, the entire gun should be wiped free of solvent and given a light film of rust-preventing oil. The grips should be wiped dry.
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — CLEANING, printed p.4

steps.title: ⛔ Routine cleaning needs no disassembly at all
steps.action: That is the whole routine job. Charter states plainly that under normal conditions there is no need to take the revolver apart, and the deep clean below is for when something actually requires it.
steps.prose: ⛔ This is the manufacturer's own boundary, not a limitation of this guide. A Charter revolver is cleaned assembled.
steps.quote: Under normal conditions, there is no need for disassembly of your revolver.
steps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Unloaded first, in capitals
deepSteps.action: Before a single screw turns, confirm the revolver is completely unloaded — cylinder out, every chamber checked by eye.
deepSteps.prose: Charter prints this as step 1 of the disassembly in capitals. The steps that follow put a cocked hammer and a compressed mainspring in your hands. Charter also says not to attempt them wearing gloves, or with your hands impeded in any way.
deepSteps.quote: FIRST AND MOST IMPORTANT, MAKE SURE THE REVOLVER IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED.
deepSteps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4

deepSteps.title: Grips off — the screw is the drift
deepSteps.action: Unscrew the grip screw until it stands well proud of the left grip, then tap the protruding screw inward with a light blow to break the right grip loose. Both grips then come off.
deepSteps.prose: The screw itself is the tool. Prising at the grips instead is how a wooden panel splits at the escutcheon.
deepSteps.aside: Tap the protruding Grip Screw inward with a light blow to loosen the right grip. Both grips may now be removed.
deepSteps.quote: Unscrew the Grip Screw until it protrudes well above the surface of the left grip.
deepSteps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Cock the hammer, then PIN the mainspring before it moves
deepSteps.action: Fully cock the hammer, then push a paper clip or small pin through the hole in the bottom of the mainspring guide rod. Only then uncock the hammer — gently — and lift out the mainspring, guide rod and seat as one assembly.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ This is the step that hurts people on a revolver. The pin captures the spring's compression; without it the mainspring leaves the frame under power the moment the hammer goes down.
deepSteps.quote: Insert a paper clip or small pin through the hole in the bottom of the Mainspring Guide Rod.
deepSteps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4
deepSteps.warn: Unless this step is followed, the mainspring may fly out and cause injury.

deepSteps.title: Three fasteners, then the butt off the frame
deepSteps.action: Remove the frame assembly screw behind the hammer, the frame assembly pin below the hammer, and the cylinder stop retaining pin in front of the trigger. The butt then comes gently off the frame.
deepSteps.prose: Note which fastener came from where before they go on the bench together — a screw and a pin from opposite ends of a small frame look alike in a tray.
deepSteps.quote: Gently remove the Butt from the Frame.
deepSteps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4

deepSteps.title: Hammer out, then oil what is now reachable
deepSteps.action: Unscrew the hammer screw from the RIGHT side of the frame and lift the hammer out. Everything that moves can now take a thin film of rust-preventing oil.
deepSteps.prose: A thin film — this is a lockwork, and oil that pools in it collects the grit that makes a double-action pull gritty.
deepSteps.aside: All moving parts may now be lightly oiled with a thin film of rust-preventing oil.
deepSteps.quote: Unscrew the Hammer Screw from the right side of the Frame and remove Hammer from Frame.
deepSteps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4

deepSteps.title: A cylinder that will not spin freely — clean the crane bushing
deepSteps.action: If the cylinder does not rotate freely when swung out, the crane bushing is fouled: remove the crane screw at the front of the frame, take the cylinder assembly off the frame, and slide the crane far enough forward out of the cylinder to clean and lightly oil the bushing.
deepSteps.prose: This is the single most useful repair in the book. A binding cylinder on a carry revolver is almost always this, and it is a five-minute job rather than a trip to a gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: remove the Crane Screw at front of Frame; remove the Cylinder assembly from the Frame; and slide the Crane far enough forward out of the Cylinder to clean and lightly oil the bushing.
deepSteps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4

deepSteps.title: ⛔ One screw that is not yours — and the end of the road
deepSteps.action: Leave the cylinder latch release screw alone. It sits in the frame behind the cylinder, it is factory-adjusted flush with the breech face, and it is not an adjustment. Reassemble by reversing the steps.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Charter ends the published procedure here in as many words. Anything past this is a gunsmith's job, and altering parts voids the warranty by the book's own statement.
deepSteps.quote: The Cylinder Latch Release Screw located in the frame behind the cylinder is factory adjusted flush with the breech face and should not be tampered with.
deepSteps.cite: Charter 2000 Double Action Revolver — Operating Instructions and Safety Precautions — Instruction Folder — no form or revision code printed — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.4
deepSteps.warn: FURTHER DISASSEMBLY IS NOT RECOMMENDED. Reassemble the revolver by reversing the order of these steps.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Nitro/powder solvent on a flannel patch and rod, through the bore and EVERY chamber
Correctly sized bristle brush only if the patches will not clear it
Dry, then a light film of rust-preventing oil

cleaning.name: FRAME & CYLINDER
tasks: Wipe the whole gun free of solvent before any oil goes on
Check all pins and screws for tightness — every session
If the cylinder binds when swung out, the crane bushing is fouled

cleaning.name: GRIPS
tasks: ⛔ Wipe the grips DRY — no oil
Check the grip screw is tight
Critical moving parts take light oil without any disassembly

reassembly: The mainspring goes back with the pin still through the guide rod; remove the pin only once the assembly is seated and the hammer can be cocked.
Refit both grips and the grip screw.
Swing the cylinder out and closed, and check it locks up and rotates freely before the revolver goes away.
fncheck: Cylinder swung out and every chamber confirmed empty: close it, check the cylinder locks up, cock and carefully uncock the hammer under thumb control, and confirm the trigger returns fully forward on its own.
